alignments.note: Postpositive δέ realized by the clause-initial But.
Purpose ἵνα takes the word introducing its English clause (rule 40).
Inflected verb takes its English subject and modal auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17).
Complementizer ὅτι rendered as that.
Article to the (rule 19).
Splits from its article as a recoverable pair (rule 26).
The ASV gives man no determiner, so the article carries nothing and the case preposition stays with the noun (rules 21, 23).
Genitive noun rendered of + noun, headed on the noun (rules 17, 21).
ἔχει → hath; the ASV reorders verb and object relative to the Greek (rule 15).
Accusative object rendered by the bare noun authority.
Preposition realized by on (rule 36).
The ASV writes a determinerless on earth, so the article has no the to anchor (rules 21, 23).
Bare noun earth.
Infinitival to is the verb's own helper, no conjunction governing the clause (rules 7, 61).
Anarthrous plural noun.
Adverb τότε → then.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject pronoun; head on the lexical verb rather than the subject (rules 9, 17).
Dative article takes the determiner with the case preposition riding along, headed on the (rules 17, 21).

One Greek adjective rendered by a whole English phrase; palsy is what glosses παραλυτικός while sick of the is the supplied completion, so the head is palsy and not the formal English head sick (rules 66, 91). Heading on sick remains defensible but rests only on English syntax, which rule 17 forbids.

Circumstantial participle converted to a coordinate finite Arise; unit SBLGNT.MAT.9.6.v009 is underdetermined between r00-base and r01, and the projection's base reading is what the ASV translates here, so no textual question arises in the alignment (rule 12).

The supplied juncture and is a helper on the finite verb it introduces after the participle-to-finite conversion, never added and never on the participle it follows (rules 29, 88). Head on take, the word glossing αἴρω.
Genitive pronoun carries the English possessive.
σου occupies the determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing (rule 20).
Bare noun bed.
Expressed καί coordinating the two imperatives.
Imperative ὕπαγε → go.
Preposition realized by unto (rule 36).
The possessive thy from σου occupies the determiner slot (rule 20).
Genitive pronoun carries the English possessive, which the ASV places before the noun (rule 15).
Bare noun house.

review_notes: Three articles (s009, s012, s028) and s023 are unrepresented for two distinct reasons: s009 and s012 because the ASV writes no determiner at all (rules 21, 23), s023 and s028 because a genitive pronoun occupies the determiner slot (rule 20).
The supplied and at t028 belongs to take up under rule 88, not to the participle Arise and not added.
s019's head is palsy rather than sick on rule 66's gloss-versus-completion test; the alternative is noted in the unit.
